groups.title: Decide whether invocation-unit skill files (every SKILL.md) keep a hard 40 KB ceiling in npm test now that the per-file pins are gone
groups.body:
Defer-reason: needs-human-decision
Origin: /flow #1997 plan-time survey (flow ledger row 25; #1990's per-file-warning decision)

**Related:** #1987

## Current State

#1990 made `context-cost.js`'s per-file 40 KB check a warning tier (`overCeilingWarnings`) and gated composed bytes per compose call site instead. #1997 retired the thirteen ad-hoc per-file test pins that had been the de-facto hard gate for files without a compose call site, per its own disposition rule, recording the removal condition as `[IL-153]`. `merge-size-probe.js` — the raw 40,960 B merge-time probe on `SKILL.md` and `_shared/*.md` — has one production invocation (`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s merge-size probe) and it discloses at warn tier, never blocking. Result: no `npm test` assertion fails when `dispatch/SKILL.md` (40,948 B), `wrap-up/SKILL.md` (40,708 B), or `tidy/step-6-auto.md` (40,102 B) crosses 40,960 B. A `SKILL.md` is read whole on every invocation of its skill, so for those files the raw number *is* the per-invocation load the parent design (#1987) said to measure — the composed gate covers only files that feed a call site.

## The decision

Two coherent positions, and the parent design chose neither explicitly:

1. **Warning tier is enough.** The 40 KB figure was always a soft heuristic; the warning band in `context-cost.test.js`, the plan-audit headroom check (now composed-aware), and the merge-time disclosure are three reporting channels; a hard gate on raw bytes is what drove the sub-file fragmentation #1987 set out to reverse. Nothing to build.
2. **Invocation units keep a hard ceiling.** Add one assertion to `context-cost.test.js`: every `plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md` stays under `CEILING_BYTES` (marker-stripped) — a single central gate instead of thirteen ad-hoc pins — because a `SKILL.md` has no lazy path around its own bytes. Sub-files and `_shared` files stay warning-tier (they are either composed or lazily read). Cost: `dispatch/SKILL.md` at 12 B under would need an extraction on its next edit, which is arguably the point.

## Deliverables (if position 2)

- One test in `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js`: every `SKILL.md` under `plugin/skills/` measures under `CEILING_BYTES` via `measuredBytes`, with a discrimination fixture; `docs/donts.md`'s rewritten rules gain the one-line distinction (invocation units hard, everything else warned or composed); `[IL-153]`'s removal condition gains "except invocation units, which keep the central ceiling".

## Acceptance Criteria

- The decision is recorded on #1987 (the parent) and in `docs/incident-log.md`'s `[IL-153]` entry either way.
- If position 2: the new test is green on the current corpus and goes red on a doctored 41 KB `SKILL.md` fixture; `npm test` green apart from the tracked baseline (#1900).

groups.title: Give issue-claims.md's MCP path its two missing instructions — the add_issue_comment mirror form and the shape step 1's MCP read writes
groups.body:
Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff
Origin: /flow #1992 whole-branch review (flow ledger rows 16 and 18)

## Current State

`plugin/skills/_shared/issue-claims.md` documents a `gh`-absent (MCP) path for every claim step except two, and #1992's `transport` fencing makes the composed `claims` bundle a cloud Routine reads the *only* instruction it sees:

1. **The mirror comment has no MCP form.** `## The mirror`'s code block ends in `gh issue comment "$ISSUE" --body-file /tmp/claim-${ISSUE}.md` and nothing beside it says what an MCP run does instead — even though `_shared/github-write-transport.md`'s CRUD table already maps `Comment` → `add_issue_comment`. The block stays unconditional in the bundle precisely because removing it would delete the only guidance.
2. **"The lock" step 2 gives an MCP reader a wrong action.** Step 2 says the file from step 1 "holds the **wrapper object** `{content, sha}` from the `gh api` call's `-q` filter" and pipes it through `jq -r '.content'` — but step 1's surviving MCP bullet writes "the tool's returned content to a file", which is already the content. The same wrapper-object phrase recurs under "Authoritative: read the blob" ("never the raw `{content, sha}` wrapper object a fresh `gh api` read produces"). Under `transport=mcp` the `gh` sentence that gave the phrase its antecedent is stripped, so the instruction reads as a step to perform on content that has no wrapper.

Both passages predate #1992 (the raw file said the same); #1992 left them untouched because its acceptance proves `stripMarkers(file) === origin/main` byte identity (`[IL-144]`), which any content change breaks.

## Deliverables

- In `## The mirror`, an MCP form beside the `gh issue comment` block: `add_issue_comment` on the issue with the same rendered body, per `_shared/github-write-transport.md`'s Comment row — fenced `transport=mcp` if the `gh` block is fenced `transport=gh` at the same time, or both left unconditional; either way every citation of "The mirror" still resolves in every composition.
- In "The lock" step 2, one MCP-side sentence stating that step 1's MCP bullet already wrote the content, so the extraction applies to the `gh` read only (fence the `jq` extraction `transport=gh` only if a `transport=mcp` counterpart says what to pass to the classifier); the same clarification at the "Authoritative: read the blob" paragraph.
- `tests/issue-claims-pr-scan-composition.test.js` extended: under `mcp` the bundle contains the `add_issue_comment` form and no unqualified wrapper-object instruction; under `gh` the `jq -r '.content'` extraction stays.
- `wc -c` on the file stays under `merge-size-probe.js`'s 40,960 B raw gate (39,635 B at #1992's head — 1,325 B of headroom, which these additions must fit or pay for by extracting a section).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `PATH` without `gh` composing `--step claims` yields a bundle whose `## The mirror` section names `add_issue_comment` and whose "The lock" step 2 tells the reader what to classify without mentioning a wrapper the MCP read never produced.
- `node --test tests/issue-claims-pr-scan-composition.test.js tests/compose-markers-conformance.test.js` green, plus every suite `grep -rl issue-claims.md tests` names.
- `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/merge-size-probe.js"` (or `wc -c`) shows the file under 40,960 B.

groups.title: Reconcile a bundle PR's Fixes lines with manifest outcomes before the merge — a not-run or failed spec must never close on merge
groups.body:
Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff
Origin: reflect full (batch) from /flow #1988-#1997 consolidated close (parent run 2026-09-06T110420)

## Current State

`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` ("One `Fixes #{n}` line per record") writes one `Fixes #{m}` per `manifest.yml` `specs[].id` into the bundle PR body at run start, before any spec has run — draft-safe by design. Nothing later reconciles those lines with what the run actually built: `hooks.js spec-status` writing `not-run` or `failed` does not touch the PR body, the "Pre-merge title/description refresh" section refreshes only the title and the phase checklist, and `flow/multispec-review-console.md`'s Shared teardown step 2 tells `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 3 to put every `specs[].id` into the merge commit's `Fixes` lines. In the #1988–#1997 run, #1996 was ruled `not-run` (its go/no-go reads post-release data) and the PR body still carried `Fixes #1996` until the controller re-read the body at close-out and replaced it by hand; the merge-commit `Fixes` list had to be narrowed by hand the same way. A headless dispatch firing has no such re-read — the merge would have closed a record that never built, and the never-started claim release would then have posted on a closed issue.

## Deliverables

- In `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s pre-merge refresh: rewrite the body's `Fixes` block from `manifest.yml` — one `Fixes #{m}` per spec with `status: complete`, and one `Refs #{m} — not run/failed: {reason}` line per spec with any other status — as an unconditional `AUTO` step alongside the title/checklist refresh.
- In `flow/multispec-review-console.md` Shared teardown step 2 and `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 3: define `{issue-list}` for a bundle as the manifest's `complete` specs, never the full `specs[].id` list; the not-run/failed set is released with `never-started:`/`abandoned:` reasons in step 3 exactly as today.
- A conformance test pinning both prose sites, plus a fixture on whatever helper composes the `Fixes` block (a manifest with one `not-run` entry yields no `Fixes` line for it and one `Refs` line).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A multi-spec run with one `not-run` spec merges with `Fixes` lines only for the complete specs; the not-run record stays open after the merge and its claim releases as `never-started`.
- The pre-merge refresh log line names the rewritten `Fixes` block.

groups.title: Make the multi-spec artifact-overwrite check distinguish an append-only shared journey from an overwrite
groups.body:
Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff
Origin: /flow #1988-#1997 consolidated close (parent run 2026-09-06T110420)

## Current State

`flow/multispec-artifact-namespacing.md`'s completion check (#786) walks `git log --name-status --diff-filter=AM {base}..HEAD -- docs/journeys/ stories/` and HARD-GATEs when any path shows `A` in one commit and `M` in a later one — "a spec's journey/story artifact was silently overwritten by a later spec's write". In the #1988–#1997 run, `docs/journeys/compose-a-per-run-context-bundle-1988.md` was added by #1988 and then modified by #1989, #1991, #1992, #1993, #1995, and #1997 — each later spec appending its own numbered step and an Origin line to the one journey that documents the composer, by design (the journeys skill's own "extend the existing journey" guidance). `git log --numstat` over the range shows every cross-spec modification is append-only (0 deletions) and every commit with deletions (at most 2 lines) edits that spec's own step or the frontmatter file list. The check cannot tell this shape from an overwrite and fires on it, so the controller had to rule it manually with the numstat as evidence.

## Deliverables

- Extend the check: for each `A`-then-`M` path, read `git log --numstat` for the later commits; a later commit whose deletions on that path are zero (or confined to lines that commit itself added earlier — a same-spec edit, identified by the `refs #N` trailer matching the step's Origin line) is an extension, not an overwrite; only a later-spec commit that deletes lines it did not add trips the gate.
- State the rule in `flow/multispec-artifact-namespacing.md` next to the existing walk, with the run above as the worked example.
- A fixture test on the walk (a synthetic repo with an add-then-append history and an add-then-overwrite history) proving the gate fires only on the second.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The #1988–#1997 history (`4c6e76733..b247a02d3`, `docs/journeys/compose-a-per-run-context-bundle-1988.md`) passes the extended check with no manual ruling.

Add a new deny gate in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` that denies a subagent's `Read` (or a Bash `cat`/`sed`/`head` invocation) of a `plugin/skills/_shared/**/*.md` path when the current run's `{run}/context/` directory already holds a composed bundle for the specific step currently in progress (the per-step condition governs everywhere in this record — Deliverables/AC below use "current run" loosely in a couple of places; read every such instance as "for the current step," since a run can have multiple steps and multiple bundles, and the gate must key off the one the current tool call's step actually needs, not merely "some bundle exists somewhere in this run") — enforcement for the boundary U8 established by convention alone. The first deliverable is explicitly a go/no-go check against U8 (#1995)'s own before/after measurement (reported in #1995's own last Deliverable and PR description): if U8 already achieved the ≥10× subagent-read reduction it targets, this record closes as not-needed, with the numbers quoted in the closing comment, rather than shipping an enforcement gate nothing further requires. That close is a snapshot judgment against U8's measured sessions, not a permanent guarantee — a later regression in subagent behavior that reintroduces heavy `_shared/` reads is a new record, evaluated fresh against then-current numbers, not an automatic reopening of this one.

**Complexity:** Low
**Estimated tasks:** 4

## Non-Goals

- Building the measurement this record's go/no-go decision consumes — that measurement is U8's own Deliverable, already produced before this record starts (Blocked by U8).
- Denying any Read/Bash access outside the exact shape described below — a subagent's Read of any other path, or a main-agent's Read of anything, is never touched by this gate.
- Fixing #1894, #1501, or #1441 — all three also edit `pre-tool-use.js`; this record's gate is additive and must not collide with any of them, but resolving those records is out of scope here.

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` already carries a family of scoping exemptions on its deny gates (`isPipelineBookkeeping`, `isPolicyFile`/`realTarget`, `isPolicyOnlyCommit`, `isDeleteOnlyPush`, `isStampsGateExemptTarget`, the Bash foreign-repos branch, `checkBookkeepingStampsGate`'s file-tool foreign-target branch) — this record's new gate must follow the same discipline every existing exemption in this file already obeys (absolute-path-only guard, resolve the leaf symlink before deciding, fail closed on every unprovable answer, a Bash-shaped exemption matches the entire command string against a grammar, every new exemption needs a regression test proven to fail on revert).
- This record's `Blocked by` link is U8 (#1995) — verify it has actually merged (e.g. `gh pr list --search "1995" --state merged`) before starting; once merged, its PR description carries the before/after subagent-read measurement for the switched dispatch prompts — this record's first real deliverable is reading that number, not writing code, before anything else here happens.
- No existing check in `pre-tool-use.js` currently reads a subagent-vs-main-agent discriminator field from the PreToolUse hook payload (a `grep -n "transcript\|isSubagent" plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` at spec time returns nothing) — the only confirmed subagent-identifying field in this codebase's hooks lives on the separate `SubagentStop` event, not `PreToolUse`. Treat "the calling context is a subagent" as an empirical Task-0 question, not a settled fact: at implementation time, inspect the actual PreToolUse hook payload shape (dump it from a real subagent-originated tool call) to confirm whether a usable field exists; if none does, this record's first code task is adding one to the hook dispatcher (`plugin/bin/hooks.js`) before the gate itself can be written, and that added-field work becomes part of this record's own scope, not a silent assumption.
- `docs/hooks.md` documents the existing gate family; this record adds this gate's own entry there.
- #1894, #1501, and #1441 are open, unscored/`needs:decision` records that also edit `pre-tool-use.js` — check each one's current state (`gh issue view` / `gh pr list`) before starting, and rebase this record's new gate onto whichever of them lands first, per the same rebase discipline U2 established.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Go/no-go read (do this first, before any code):** read U8's reported before/after subagent-read numbers for the switched shared-contract files. If U8 already achieved a ≥10× reduction (its own stated target), close this record as not-needed: post a closing comment quoting U8's exact before/after numbers and the reasoning that the enforcement gate is not required, and stop — none of the deliverables below are built.
- [ ] (If the go/no-go above says "still needed") A new deny gate, `checkSharedSkillReadGate` (or the sibling-check naming convention this file already uses), firing only when: (a) the tool is `Read`, or a Bash invocation whose ENTIRE command string is exactly one of `cat <path>`, `sed ... <path>`, or `head ... <path>` against a single `plugin/skills/_shared/**/*.md` path (no pipe, `&&`/`;` chaining, redirection, or multi-file argument — any of those shapes falls through ungated as an accepted, documented limitation of this gate's first version, not silently swallowed); (b) the calling context is a subagent, confirmed via whatever field the Task-0 payload inspection above establishes (fail CLOSED on this condition specifically: a call this gate cannot conclusively classify as subagent-originated — including the fork case, which inherits the orchestrator's own session id and identity — is treated as NOT a subagent and is never denied, per this file's existing indeterminate-fails-closed discipline; a fixture test proves the fork case passes through ungated); and (c) `{run}/context/{step}.md` exists for the specific step the current tool call belongs to (the bundle filename pattern U1 (#1988) defines — not merely "some file exists under `{run}/context/`").
- [ ] Deny message names the specific bundle path the subagent should read instead.
- [ ] Enumerate, at plan time, every sanctioned caller of a `_shared/**` Read from a subagent context and every non-destructive/safe mode of the gated tool (per `spec-template.md`'s Gate-Authoring Deliverables) — confirm none is denied by the proposed condition before implementation begins. Record this enumerated list durably in `docs/hooks.md` itself (a roster table alongside the gate's own entry), not only in a plan file that may not survive past this record's own PR merging.
- [ ] Apply the absolute-path-only guard, leaf-symlink resolution (mirroring `realTarget()`), and fail-closed-on-indeterminate discipline this file's existing gates already establish — reuse the existing helpers, don't reimplement them.
- [ ] Fixture regression tests for each sanctioned caller enumerated above, proving they pass through the gate untouched, plus a test proving the gate denies the exact shape it targets and nothing broader — every new test proven to fail on revert (`git checkout -- {file}` on the implementation only, confirm only the new test goes red, then restore).
- [ ] `docs/hooks.md` gains this gate's entry, following the existing documentation convention for the gate family.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. If the go/no-go read finds U8 already achieved its target: this record closes with a comment quoting the numbers, and no code ships.
2. If the gate ships: it denies the enumerated shape (subagent + `_shared/**` Read/single-file cat-sed-head + an existing bundle for the current step) and only that shape — proven by fixture tests for each sanctioned caller passing through untouched, plus a fixture proving a piped/chained/multi-file Bash invocation of the same three verbs passes through ungated (the documented first-version limitation).
3. The gate never fires in the main agent, never fires on a fork (which is treated as indeterminate-subagent-status and fails closed, per the fail-closed discipline), and never fires when no bundle exists for the current step — proven by fixture tests for all three cases.
4. `docs/hooks.md` documents the gate.
5. `npm test` passes, including every new fixture test, each shown to fail on revert of the implementation alone.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — edit (only if the gate ships): add the new deny gate following the existing exemption discipline.
- `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js` (or the sibling suite that already covers this gate family — confirm the exact file at plan time rather than assuming this name) — edit: add fixture tests for the gate and every sanctioned caller.
- `docs/hooks.md` — edit (only if the gate ships): document the new gate.

## Gotchas

- Read U8's numbers before writing any code — this record's very first deliverable can end the record entirely; do not start on the gate implementation until that read has actually happened and the decision is recorded.
- Every unprovable answer in this file fails CLOSED, and a conclusive exemption must never be gated on an unrelated inconclusive one (`[IL-149]`) — `wtDetect.repoInfo()`/`mainCheckoutRoot()` returning `indeterminate: true` or `null` is a different fact from a definitive negative, never read as "not applicable."
- Resolve the leaf symlink before deciding, mirroring `realTarget()` (`[IL-150]`) — a path-based decision made on the raw literal target can be defeated by a symlink whose target resolves outside the intended scope; never call a path-answering function on a literal path without checking for a leaf symlink first.
- A Bash-shaped exemption (or, here, a Bash-shaped deny condition) must match the ENTIRE command string against a grammar — no partial match on a flag or filename lets a differently-shaped command slip past. Prove the staged set with `git diff --name-status`, never `--name-only`, when verifying the fix's own diff.
- #1894, #1501, and #1441 all edit `pre-tool-use.js` — rebase this record's new gate onto whichever lands first, and re-run the sanctioned-caller enumeration against the current file state at implementation time, not against a stale read from spec time.
- Every new exemption/gate needs a regression test proven to fail on revert — a green suite alone is not evidence the test discriminates; this is the same discipline the pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions skill documents for every existing gate in this file.

This record is Phase 5 of #1987 (Skill context composer — per-run bundles composed by resolved condition, not per-file ceilings): #1987's Phases 1-4 ship the composer mechanism and its per-step measurement; this record consumes that measurement and does the prose-diet and scaffolding-dedupe pass on top of it.

## Technical Approach

groups.title: init: Port Isolation step — detect literal ports, propose the env rewrite, set port-services
groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Overview

The injection half, made a one-time `/init` step. After Step 6 (Worktree Configuration), a new Step 6.5 detects literal dev-server ports in the project's config, presents a reviewable rewrite diff that replaces each literal with an env read defaulting to the old value, queues `port-services` for the deferred write to `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` (same mechanism as `worktree-always`), adds `.env.local`/`.env` to the gitignore suggestions, and runs the first `allocate`. Known-hard cases are reported for manual action, never rewritten. Update mode reports drift (a literal port that crept back in).

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 5

## Non-Goals

- The registry/CLI/hook (Units 1-3)
- dev-url-detection (Unit 5)
- Rewriting anything the table below marks report-only
- Running the project's dev server

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/init/SKILL.md` Phase 0 lists Steps 1-20 as 2-4-line stubs each pointing at `bootstrap/step-NN-*.md` (`step-08-5-dependency-read-permissions.md` is the existing half-step naming precedent).
- Step 4 (`bootstrap/step-04-gitignore-suggestions.md`) owns gitignore suggestions and "never modify `.gitignore` without asking".
- Step 6 queues the `worktree-always` policy write and defers it to "Finalizing the worktree-always Decision" (`worktree-policy-finalization.md`) — the same deferral mechanism must carry `port-services`, since a `worktree-always` run denies its own later writes.
- Detection inputs already enumerated in `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` Step 2 (CLAUDE.md Commands, package.json scripts, `vite.config.*` `server.port`, `next.config.*`, `angular.json`, `vue.config.*`, `.env`/`.env.local` `PORT=`).
- Update mode: `plugin/skills/init/update-mode.md` (drift report).
- `docs/skill-graph.md` `## init` section holds every init edge; `docs/getting-started.md` is the user-facing walkthrough.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `plugin/skills/init/bootstrap/step-06-5-port-isolation.md` (new) containing: the detection list (dev-url-detection's Step 2 list plus `docker-compose.yml`/`compose.yml` host `ports:` mappings, `app.listen(<int>)`/`.listen(<int>)` in JS/TS server entry files, `runserver <int>`/`uvicorn --port <int>`/`flask run -p <int>` in README/Makefile/scripts — see `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-02-port-isolation-design.md` Section 4 for the source table this deliverable transposes verbatim, before that doc is deleted), the rewrite table (before → after) exactly as the design doc's Section 4 table, the report-only hard cases (shell expansion in `package.json` scripts — no Windows `cmd` support; `angular.json` `serve.options.port` cannot read env; literal ports in README/Makefile Python commands) plus a catch-all: a detected literal port matching none of the six rewrite rows and none of the three named hard cases defaults to report-only, never a guessed rewrite; the service-name derivation (`web` for the frontend dev server, `api` for a backend, `db` for a Compose database, confirmed via one `AskUserQuestion` listing the detected services with Recommended pre-filled; a second service in the same category gets a numeric suffix — `web2`, `api2` — offered as a pre-filled option in the same `AskUserQuestion` rather than silently colliding), a zero-detected-services outcome (no config file matches the detection list — Step 6.5 reports nothing found and skips the rewrite/`port-services`/`allocate` sequence entirely; no policy write, no lease), the syntax-validity check on every proposed rewrite before it is shown in the diff (parse the rewritten JS/TS/YAML/Compose snippet with the language's own parser; a snippet that fails to parse is downgraded to report-only for that location rather than offered in the diff), the reviewable-diff gate (one `AskUserQuestion`: Apply all / Choose files / Skip rewrite — every mode, including auto, because it edits the user's own config outside the always-reversible floor; a declined rewrite still sets `port-services` and leases a block *from the free pool*, not matched to whatever literal port remains hardcoded — the resulting mismatch between the registry's block and the surviving literal is exactly what `update-mode.md`'s port-literal-drift check exists to catch on a later run), and the first `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/ports.js" allocate --services {list}` run with the resulting block echoed.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/init/SKILL.md`: a `### Step 6.5: Port Isolation` stub (≤ 4 lines) after Step 6, plus a one-line entry in the "Phases at a Glance" table if it enumerates steps; the `port-services` write joins the deferred-write mechanism named in "Finalizing the worktree-always Decision".
- [ ] `plugin/skills/init/worktree-policy-finalization.md`: add `port-services` to the deferred-write list this file already carries `worktree-always` through, so Step 6.5's policy write queues here exactly like `worktree-always`'s does rather than firing directly.
- [ ] `bootstrap/step-04-gitignore-suggestions.md`: `.env.local` and `.env` added to the suggested block with a one-line reason (managed ports region).
- [ ] `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`: add the Step 6.5 rewrite-diff gate to the HARD-GATE exemption list (it must stop even in `auto`, matching the existing `.gitignore`-write-style exemption already enumerated there) — per this file's own "Adding a new policy lever" checklist item for gates that stop in every mode.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/init/update-mode.md`: one drift row — a file from the detection list containing a literal port where the rewrite was previously applied → "port literal drift" finding pointing at Step 6.5.
- [ ] `docs/skill-graph.md` `## init`: one edge row `bin/ports.js` (Step 6.5 runs the first allocate) and one `_shared/dev-url-detection.md` row (Step 6.5 reuses its Step 2 detection list, read live).
- [ ] `docs/getting-started.md`: one short paragraph on port isolation (what `port-services` does, where the block shows up).
- [ ] `tests/init-port-isolation-conformance.test.js` (new prose test).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `init/SKILL.md` contains a `### Step 6.5: Port Isolation` heading between Step 6 and Step 7 whose body cites `bootstrap/step-06-5-port-isolation.md`; the sub-file contains the rewrite table with all six rows from the design doc and the three report-only hard cases by name (Windows `cmd` shell expansion, `angular.json`, README/Makefile Python commands).
2. The sub-file states the diff gate runs in every mode including `auto`, and that a declined rewrite still writes `port-services` and runs `allocate`.
3. The `port-services` write is routed through the same deferred-write mechanism as `worktree-always` (the sub-file names "Finalizing the worktree-always Decision" and `worktree-policy-finalization.md` names `port-services`).
4. `step-04-gitignore-suggestions.md` lists `.env.local` and `.env`.
5. `update-mode.md` contains the port-literal drift row; `docs/skill-graph.md` `## init` has the two new rows; `docs/getting-started.md` mentions `port-services`.
6. `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` passes — `init/SKILL.md` gains no more than the stub (it is already at 41,360 B; see Gotchas).
7. A byte-pinned snippet test runs the `allocate` command line from the sub-file against a tmp `home` and asserts exit 0 (proves the documented command is executable, per `skill-prose-conformance-tests`) — this test, and Step 6.5 itself, are blocked on #1791 and #1792 shipping first (this unit only consumes `bin/ports.js` and `port-services`; it does not build either).
8. The sub-file states a rewrite is syntax-checked before being shown in the diff, and that a snippet failing that check falls back to report-only rather than being offered.

## Technical Approach

All detection and rewrite logic is LLM-driven skill prose (grep/read/propose), in line with every other `/init` step; the only executable is Unit 1's CLI. groups.title: blast-radius.js should exclude pipeline-artifact paths from implLines/implFiles counting
groups.body:
Origin: reflect light from #1535
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`bin/blast-radius.js`'s `summary.implLines`/`summary.implFiles` count every non-test file in the diff as implementation, with no carve-out for this pipeline's own generated process artifacts: a materialized spec (`{run-dir}/work/{n}-spec.md`) and a `superpowers:writing-plans` implementation plan doc (`docs/superpowers/plans/*.md`). On #1535 — a genuinely 1-line production fix in `plugin/bin/build-review-context.js` plus a 21-line test — the tool reported `implLines: 152`, `implFiles: 3` against a configured guideline of `auto-merge-max-lines: 40`/`auto-merge-max-files: 2`, purely because the 39-line spec and 111-line plan doc were counted alongside the actual code change.

`merge-check.md`'s Step 2 explicitly asks the judge to weigh `implLines`/`implFiles` against the guideline "once the diff is judged to carry behavior change" — but the tool hands over a number that conflates pipeline bookkeeping with real implementation risk, forcing every merge-check invocation on a record with a materialized header to manually discount the spec/plan doc's line count before the comparison means anything. That manual discount is easy to get wrong or skip under time pressure, and skipping it would make a genuinely tiny, low-risk fix look artificially large enough to lean `needs-human`.

## Deliverables

- In `plugin/bin/lib/issues/blast-radius.js` (or wherever `summary` is computed), exclude paths matching `${RUN_DIR}/work/*-spec.md` (the materialized-header convention, `flow/materialize.md`) and `docs/superpowers/plans/*.md` (the `superpowers:writing-plans` convention) from `implLines`/`implFiles`/the file classification that feeds them — the same way test files are already split out into `testLines`/`testFiles`.
- Confirm `merge-check.md`'s Step 2 prose still reads correctly once the counts it consumes no longer include pipeline artifacts (no prose change expected, since the judge already treats the numbers as inputs, not ground truth).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `node bin/blast-radius.js --integration-branch <ref>` run against a diff containing only a materialized spec + plan doc (no real code) reports `implLines: 0`, `implFiles: 0`.
2. Existing `blast-radius`/`merge-check` tests continue to pass with the narrower classification.

## Original request

Surfaced during #1535's own wrap-up (Reflect, light mode, Fresh-start lens) — evidence is that run's own `blast-radius.js` output: `{"summary":{"implLines":152,"implFiles":3,"testLines":21,"testFiles":1}}` for a 1-line production change.

groups.title: Add conformance test banning process.exit() inside require.main guards in plugin/bin/**/*.js
groups.body:
## Current State

Three separate records have now each closed the identical `process.exit(run(...))` compute-then-exit stdout-truncation idiom in a different `plugin/bin/*.js` file: #1176, #1313, and #1535. Each was found by a manual `process.exit(` grep sweep over `plugin/bin/*.js` — and each sweep missed at least one file the previous sweep had already missed, since the violation this record (#1535) fixed was only discovered as a byproduct of #1313's own final whole-branch review. The contract this idiom violates is already documented — `plugin/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/SKILL.md`'s CLI wrapper contract section states the `require.main === module` guard must set `process.exitCode = run(...)`, never call `process.exit()` directly, because the latter can truncate a pending stdout write for a piped consumer — but nothing enforces it mechanically. A fourth recurrence is only a matter of time without a mechanical check.

#1535's final whole-branch review (opus, high effort) verified two existing exceptions to the rule are safe and should be allowlisted rather than flagged: `plugin/bin/hooks.js:1273` (`main(process.argv).then((code) => process.exit(code)).catch(() => process.exit(0));` — all of this file's own stdout goes through `fs.writeSync(1, ...)`, a synchronous call with nothing pending to flush) and `plugin/bin/lib/statusline-wrapper-source.js` (a wrapper that deliberately hard-stops on the child process's own exit code — the hard stop is the intended behavior, not a bug).

## Deliverables

- Add a `node --test` conformance test (e.g. `tests/bin-lib/exit-code-conformance.test.js`) that walks `plugin/bin/**/*.js`, finds each `require.main === module` (or equivalent) entry-point guard, and fails if that guard calls `process.exit(...)` directly instead of assigning `process.exitCode = ...`.
- Allowlist exactly two entries, both re-verified against the current file content at implementation time (not just copied from this record): `plugin/bin/hooks.js` and `plugin/bin/lib/statusline-wrapper-source.js`.
- Confirm the test fails (red) against a synthetic fixture carrying the violating idiom before wiring it against the real `plugin/bin/**/*.js` tree, per this repo's TDD convention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The new conformance test passes against the current `plugin/bin/**/*.js` tree with exactly the two allowlisted exceptions above and no others.
2. Reverting either #1313's or #1535's fix (reintroducing `process.exit(run(...))` in the affected file) makes the new test fail.
3. `npm test` passes in full.

## Original request

Surfaced as a Recommendation (not actioned, out of scope) in #1535's final whole-branch review: "Replace the manual sweep with a mechanical check. This is the third record (#1176 → #1313 → #1535) closing the same violation of a contract that is already written down, each time via a hand-run grep that was incomplete the previous two times."

groups.title: dev-url-detection: lease-first probe, lease-based MATCH/FOREIGN, ephemeral start on the leased block
groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Overview

Makes the pipeline's own browser work use the same block the human's terminal uses. `_shared/dev-url-detection.md` gains a Step 0.5 that probes `http://localhost:{PORT}` from this checkout's lease first; Step 2.7's worktree check becomes lease-based (a responding port is MATCH iff it is in this checkout's lease), demoting the POSIX-only `lsof` heuristic to the no-lease fallback; "Ephemeral server start" uses the leased block and passes the managed env through instead of probing upward; wrap-up Section D stops the server by PID and no longer needs `lsof` when a lease exists.

**Complexity:** Low
**Estimated tasks:** 4

## Non-Goals

- Any code change (Units 1-3 own the CLI/hook/statusline)
- `/init`
- Changing which skills call this procedure
- Removing the `lsof` fallback for unleased projects

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` — Step 0 (persisted `stories/servers.yml`), Step 1 (probe common ports), Step 2 (config), Step 2.7 (worktree awareness via `lsof` PID→cwd comparison; the `repoInfo()` linked-worktree check via `bin/lib/hooks/worktree-detect.js` stays), Step 3 (resolve; "Ephemeral server start" probes upward from the framework default and records `{run-dir}/ephemeral-server.txt` as `{pid} {port} {worktree-root}`), Step 4 (persist), Cleanup.
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section D reads `ephemeral-server.txt`, `kill {pid}`, falls back to `lsof -ti tcp:{port} | xargs kill`.
- Consumers of the procedure: `/stories`, `/test`, `/flow`, `/visual-review`, `/demo` (listed in the file's header — none need edits; the procedure's outputs `APP_URL`/`SERVER_STARTED` are unchanged).

## Deliverables

- [ ] Step 0.5 "Lease-first probe": run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/ports.js" env` in the checkout; when no lease exists for this checkout, the command prints nothing and exits 0 (#1791's own contract for that case) — treat that as "no lease," fall through to Step 1. Otherwise parse every printed `KEY=value` line into `LEASE_PORTS` (the full set of port *values* across all lines — `PORT`, and every `{NAME}_PORT`, not just `PORT`); HTTP-probe `http://localhost:{PORT}` (the value from the `PORT` line specifically) with the Step 1 check; on 2xx/3xx set `APP_URL` and skip Steps 1-2.7 (the lease *is* the worktree-awareness proof); on no response continue to Step 1 with `LEASE_PORTS` (the full set already parsed) remembered.
- [ ] Step 2.7 rewritten: when `LEASE_PORTS` is set, MATCH iff the responding port ∈ `LEASE_PORTS`, else FOREIGN — no `lsof`; when no lease, the existing `lsof` block stays, now explicitly labelled POSIX-only with the Windows outcome stated (PID unresolvable → FOREIGN, i.e. start an ephemeral server) — this is an accepted, stated trade-off: on Windows, an unleased project never reuses an already-running dev server and always starts a fresh ephemeral one, unlike POSIX where `lsof` can still find a same-cwd match.
- [ ] "Ephemeral server start" step 1 replaced: with a lease, re-run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/ports.js" env` at start time (not the value cached from Step 0.5, to avoid acting on a stale snapshot) for `PORT` and pass every printed `KEY=value` line into the spawned server's environment verbatim — no allowlist beyond "whatever this checkout's own managed region currently contains" — so sibling services resolve to their own block; without a lease, keep the probe-upward rule. `ephemeral-server.txt` gains no new fields.
- [ ] Step 0's persisted-URL acceptance updated to the same lease-first rule: a persisted `stories/servers.yml` URL is accepted only when its port is a member of this checkout's `LEASE_PORTS` (or, with no lease, passes the existing worktree-awareness check); on mismatch, discard the persisted URL and fall through to Step 1's fresh probe rather than trusting it. Cleanup's standalone kill updated the same way (`kill {pid}` from `ephemeral-server.txt`; `lsof` fallback only when no lease) — cleanup always trusts the PID captured in `ephemeral-server.txt` at start time and never re-reads the live lease, so a lease that has since changed or expired cannot desync the kill.
- [ ] wrap-up Section D: `lsof` fallback wording qualified as no-lease/POSIX-only; with a lease the port is known and the PID kill is sufficient.
- [ ] `tests/dev-url-detection-lease-conformance.test.js` (new prose test) proving each assertion can go red per `skill-prose-conformance-tests`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `dev-url-detection.md` contains a `### Step 0.5` heading whose body invokes `bin/ports.js env` and states the skip rule for Steps 1-2.7 on a responding leased port.
2. Step 2.7's MATCH rule is stated in terms of `LEASE_PORTS` membership, and the `lsof` block is inside an explicit "no lease" branch labelled POSIX-only with the Windows outcome (FOREIGN → ephemeral start).
3. "Ephemeral server start" names the managed env pass-through and no longer says "probe upward" for the leased case.
4. Section D of `cleanup-procedures-execution.md` qualifies the `lsof` fallback as no-lease only.
5. The procedure's `## Output` variables are unchanged (`APP_URL`, `SERVER_STARTED`) — the conformance test asserts the Output table is byte-identical to today's.
6. `dev-url-detection.md` stays under the 40 KB ceiling (11.6 KB today).

## Technical Approach

Prose-only change to a `_shared` contract with five consumers — follow the repo's `shared-contract-extraction` skill's consumer-migration discipline for the citation sweep (grep every consumer for "Step 2.7"/"lsof"/"probe upward" and confirm none restates the retired mechanics).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` — Step 0.5, 2.7, ephemeral start, cleanup
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — Section D
- `tests/dev-url-detection-lease-conformance.test.js` — new

### Package Dependencies

- none

## Gotchas

- `cleanup-procedures-execution.md` is also edited by Unit 3 (Section C) — this unit is Blocked by Unit 3; rebase before editing.
- Keep `stories/servers.yml` semantics: a persisted URL is still subject to the lease MATCH rule, never trusted on its own.
- The `worktree-detect.js` `repoInfo()` check stays as the linked-worktree detector; only the PID→cwd comparison is replaced.
- The procedure's "Permissions required" note (writes in Step 4) is unchanged.
- This unit's interface with `bin/ports.js env` is pinned by #1791 AC12 (leased path: managed lines only; no lease: prints nothing, exits 0) — that contract, not this record, is authoritative if the two ever disagree; this unit is Blocked by #1791 (and #1792, #1793) precisely because it consumes that CLI and `port-services` without building either.
- Lease membership is accepted as sufficient proof of MATCH with no PID-level cross-check, unlike the retained `lsof` no-lease path — this is a deliberate trade-off, not an oversight: a lease can theoretically go stale between a process dying and Unit 1's gc or Unit 3's reap clearing it, but that window is no wider than the gaps `lsof`'s own PID→cwd comparison already has, and the lease-first path is what makes worktree-awareness work at all on Windows.

## Decision Rationale

See #1791 Decision Rationale — in short: a machine-wide lease registry (chosen over a path-hash or OS-assigned-port-0 scheme) hands each checkout a verified-free 10-port block; this unit makes the pipeline's own browser tooling prefer that same block over guessing, so a human's terminal and the pipeline's ephemeral server never disagree about which backend a frontend is proxying to.

groups.title: ports: statusline segment and lease release at every worktree-removal site
groups.body:
Surface: backend

**Related:** #1235

## Overview

Makes each terminal show its own ports and stops leases from outliving their worktrees. A statusline segment renders the block base for the current cwd; both worktree reapers and the two skill-driven removal sites release the lease after a successful `git worktree remove`. Release failure is logged, never fatal — Unit 1's gc is the backstop.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 6

## Non-Goals

- SessionStart/ensure (Unit 2)
- `/init`
- dev-url-detection
- Changing any reaper eligibility predicate (release runs only after a removal the existing predicate already approved)

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/claude-tweaks-statusline.js` builds `segments = [renderProject, renderModel, renderContext, renderEffort, renderGit, renderRateLimit×2, findActiveSpec, findOpenLedger, renderAccount].filter(...)` joined by `SEPARATOR`; each renderer returns `''`/null when inapplicable; tests in `tests/statusline.test.js` and `tests/install-statusline-wrapper.test.js` (the wrapper source `plugin/bin/lib/statusline-wrapper-source.js` is byte-pinned — do not touch it).
- Reapers: `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js` `reapWorktrees()` calls `runGit(['worktree','remove', real], root)` (~line 284) and `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` `reapMerged()` does the same (~line 133); both fail closed and are tested by `tests/hooks-worktree-reap.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` with frozen fixtures.
- Skill-side removal: `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` line ~154 and `plugin/skills/tidy/SKILL.md` line ~165 (`git -C "{REPO_ROOT}" worktree remove {path}`), and `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section C (worktree teardown, `ExitWorktree` for own cwd).

## Deliverables

- [ ] `renderPorts(cwd, {home})` in `claude-tweaks-statusline.js`: reads the registry degrade-open, finds the lease whose `path` equals the realpath of the git toplevel of `cwd` (walk up to the nearest `.git` file/dir rather than spawning git — the statusline must stay spawn-free beyond what it already does; for a linked worktree the nearest `.git` is a *file* pointing at the real gitdir, not a directory — the toplevel is still the directory containing that `.git` file, not a path derived from the gitdir it points to, and the result must be realpath'd with the exact same normalization Unit 1's `registry.allocate`/`registryPath` uses for `path` — same casing, same symlink resolution — or a leased worktree's segment silently never matches), renders `:{base}` (e.g. `:20010`), `''` when none; inserted after `renderGit`. The registry read (including a present-but-malformed/throwing `readRegistry`, not just a missing `ports` module) is wrapped in one try/catch that degrades to `''` — AC1's "unreadable registry ⇒ byte-identical output" covers both the missing-module and the bad-data case, not just the require.
- [ ] `release(real, {home})` — imported from Unit 1's `plugin/bin/lib/ports/registry.js` (#1791) — call in both reapers immediately after a successful `worktree remove` (rm exit 0), wrapped so a throw is recorded in the result as `portsRelease: 'failed: {msg}'` and never changes the reap outcome. `release` on a path with no lease (not every worktree acquires one — Unit 2/`ensure` is out of scope here) is a no-op that reports nothing, matching #1791 AC6's release contract — this is the common case, not the exceptional one. Use one consistent identifier for the seam across the Deliverable and Technical Approach — the injectable option key is `releasePorts`, defaulting to `release` from `registry.js`; a test's injected spy binds to `releasePorts`, never to a separately-named `release`.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` + `plugin/skills/tidy/SKILL.md`: one added line each after the `worktree remove` instruction: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/ports.js" release --path {path}` (best-effort: on failure, print to stderr only — never blocks the finding, and no other visibility surface exists for the skill-side call, unlike the reaper's structured `portsRelease` field).
- [ ] `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section C: the same release line as the step after removal, always with an explicit `--path {path}` flag rather than relying on the CLI's cwd-based default — `release(path)` only needs the path string, not a live process cwd, but the CLI's automatic `--path` default (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of cwd) stops resolving once the worktree directory is gone or the session has `cd`'d out of it. Passing `--path` explicitly removes the ordering dependency: for the own-cwd path, release the captured worktree path either just before or just after `ExitWorktree` — the explicit flag makes both orders equally correct.
- [ ] Tests for each of the above.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Statusline with a registry leasing the test cwd's toplevel renders a `:20010` segment between the git and rate-limit segments; with no registry, no lease, or an unreadable registry, output is byte-identical to today. Includes a linked-worktree fixture (a `.git` file, not directory) proving the toplevel resolution matches the registry's own realpath normalization.
2. `reapWorktrees` on a fixture where removal succeeds calls the injected `releasePorts` spy with the removed realpath; when removal fails, it is not called; when it throws, the reap result is unchanged except for the `portsRelease` note; when the removed path had no lease, it returns its no-op success with no note.
3. Same four cases for `reapMerged`.
4. Prose conformance tests (per the repo's `skill-prose-conformance-tests` skill): the release line is present after each of the three skill-side `worktree remove` sites, and the wrap-up own-cwd ordering (release before `ExitWorktree`) is stated.
5. `tests/install-statusline-wrapper.test.js` still passes unchanged.

## Technical Approach

Statusline reads `registry.readRegistry({home})` from Unit 1 (require the module lazily inside `renderPorts` so a missing module — older wrapper install — degrades to `''`). Reapers import `release` from `plugin/bin/lib/ports/registry.js` with an injectable seam `{ releasePorts = release }` in their options object, mirroring how `runGit` is injected today.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/claude-tweaks-statusline.js` — renderPorts + segment
- `tests/statusline.test.js`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js` — release after remove
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` — release after remove
- `tests/hooks-worktree-reap.test.js`
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js`
- `plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` — one line
- `plugin/skills/tidy/SKILL.md` — one line
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — Section C step
- `tests/ports-release-sites-conformance.test.js` — new prose test

### Package Dependencies

- none

## Gotchas

- `tidy/SKILL.md` (41,216 B) and `tidy/scan-procedures.md` (41,232 B) are already over the 40 KB ceiling `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` enforces — check how that test currently treats them (allowance or exemption) before adding; if the addition trips it, add the one line and trim an equal number of bytes of redundant prose in the same file rather than skipping the line.
- Reapers fail CLOSED on every predicate — release must sit strictly after the successful removal and must not introduce a new predicate.
- `reap-merged.js` overlaps open #1235 (Related, `needs:decision`); keep the edit to the lines strictly after the successful `worktree remove` call — that scoping is what makes this edit resilient to #1235's own eventual, still-undecided change landing before or after this one.
- The statusline runs on every prompt render — no `execFileSync` for git, no lock acquisition, degrade-open reads only.

## Decision Rationale

See #1791 Decision Rationale.

Surface: backend

## Current State

#647's expand phase shipped per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` (`permittedGrants`), fixing a bug where the flat top-level `reason` string could pair a granted `bornReady` with the other grant's denial text. The flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys were kept as a transitional twin, with the module header (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, lines ~10-15) recording a removal condition: delete the flat keys at the first release on or after 2026-11-16 (ship date + 3 months, per `policy-deprecations.md`'s dated-backstop shape).

Two skill-text consumers carry a matching read-side fallback, tagged with the same removal condition: `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (line ~144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (line ~223), both doing `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }`.

Confirmed at shaping time (2026-08-17): the module header text, both fallback call sites, and `skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line (`↳ trust: {provenance} / {band} — {verdict}{, {coverage}% coverage}`) all reproduce exactly as described — the trust-table snippet's `bornReady`/`reason` output fields (written to `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) are genuinely dead: nothing downstream reads or renders them.

The removal date (2026-11-16) has **not** yet passed as of this record's shaping (2026-08-17) — it is roughly three months out. This record documents and prepares the contract phase; it does not authorize building the removal before that date.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Verify, at build time, that the current date is on or after 2026-11-16 (the first release on/after that date) before making any of the changes below. If built before that date, stop without editing anything and report the record as not yet actionable — see Acceptance Criteria #1, a hard gate.
- [ ] Re-run `grep -rn "permittedGrants" skills/ bin/` to confirm every consumer still reads only `grants.*` shapes (no new flat-key consumer introduced since shaping).
- [ ] Remove the flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys from `permittedGrants`'s return value in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, and delete the module-header comment block documenting the now-resolved removal condition.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (the `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` pattern and its explanatory comment), reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (same pattern, same treatment).
- [ ] Drop the dead `bornReady`/`reason` output fields from `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet (the `node -e` block that writes `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) — confirmed nothing downstream (`skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line) reads them.
- [ ] Decide, and record the decision inline as a code/skill-text comment, how to handle the two disclosed conflation residues before deleting the flat keys:
  1. Withheld grants share one reason string today — `grants.bornAuthorized.reason` can carry born-ready's rationale on the human-filed path. Decide whether this stays as-is (the per-grant shape already fixes the *granted*-path pairing bug; the withheld-grant sharing is a separate, lower-severity residue) or gets its own follow-up record.
  2. The granted path's flat `reason` today carries positive rationale text ("class is clean, ceiling is unattended, grant origination opted in") that no per-grant key reproduces. Decide whether to populate that positive rationale into the granted per-grant `reason` field, or record explicitly (in a code comment) that it is intentionally dropped as noise once the grant itself is visible via `granted: true`.
- [ ] Update or remove the flat-key compat tests in the `bin-lib/issues` test suite to match the per-grant-only shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hard precondition, checked first:** the build only proceeds once the current date is on or after 2026-11-16. A build attempted before that date stops without modifying any file and reports the record as not yet actionable — this is not a normal "build failed" outcome, it is the record's own documented gate.
2. `permittedGrants` (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`) returns only the per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` shape — no flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys at the top level.
3. No consumer (code or skill text, across `skills/` and `bin/`) reads the flat keys or carries a fallback for them — confirmed via `grep -rn "permittedGrants" skills/ bin/` read against every hit.
4. `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet no longer computes or emits `bornReady`/`reason` fields.
5. The two conflation-residue decisions are recorded (as a comment near the code they affect, or in this record's own close-out note) — not silently dropped.
6. `npm test` passes with the flat-key compat tests updated or removed.

## Technical Approach

Start with the grep re-verification (Deliverables item 2) — the module header itself calls this out as the first step, since a consumer could have appeared between #647 shipping and this record's execution.

`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`: delete the flat keys from `permittedGrants`'s two return objects (denied-path and granted-path, around current lines 128-155) and the header comment block (lines 10-15) documenting the removal condition — the condition is satisfied, not evergreen.

`skills/capture/SKILL.md` (~line 144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (~line 223): drop the `|| { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` fallback half of each destructure, reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly; delete the accompanying "older installed build" comment.

`skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table `node -e` block (~lines 219-234): remove `bornReady`/`reason` from the `out[issue.number]` object literal.

Fold the two conflation-residue decisions into the same edit pass — they're small text/comment changes, not separate work.

Grep the `bin-lib/issues` test directory for `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized` flat-key assertions on `permittedGrants`'s return value and update/remove them alongside the source change, in the same commit.

## Gotchas

- **Date gate is load-bearing, not advisory.** This record was shaped on 2026-08-17, roughly three months before the 2026-11-16 backstop. Confirmed by reading `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`'s own module header, which states the removal condition explicitly and cites `policy-deprecations.md`'s dated-backstop shape as precedent for this pattern (see also #628/#629, which apply the same shape to `policy.yml` key retirements). Marking this record `ready` reflects that it is *shaped* and *queued*, not that it is *buildable today* — `/specify` has no mechanism to hold a record out of `ready` pending a future calendar date (only `parked` + `Trigger:` does that, and only `/tidy`/`/wrap-up`/`/reflect`/`/review`'s Defer paths can add it), so this Gotcha and Acceptance Criterion 1 are the only gate. Whoever dispatches this record (`/flow`, `/build`, or a human) must re-check the date before touching code.
- **Information loss is real if the conflation residues are skipped.** Deleting the flat keys without deciding the two residues (the Deliverables item above them) silently drops the granted-path's positive rationale text — no per-grant key reproduces it today. This isn't a formatting nit; a human reading a future trust/grant explanation loses the "why" for a clean grant unless this is deliberately decided and recorded.
- **Verified against live code at shaping time**, not taken on faith from the issue text: read `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` lines 1-40 (module header and `permittedGrants`), `skills/capture/SKILL.md` line ~144, `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` lines ~203-235, and `skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md` lines ~75-100 (the rendered trust-consequence template, confirming it never references `bornReady`/`reason`). All three deliverables reproduce exactly as the original request states — no false premise to correct here.
